quotes.t: I am allowed to start again today. Yesterday taught me something, and I carry the lesson, not the weight. This morning is mine to shape.
I am doing better than I give myself credit for. Small steps still move me forward. I will notice my progress today, not just the distance left.
My worth is not measured by how much I get done. I am enough as I am, right now. Rest is part of my strength, not a break from it.
I can hold hard feelings without being ruled by them. They visit, and they pass. I am the sky, not the weather.
I trust myself to handle what today brings. I have faced difficult days before and found my way through. I will find my way again.
I speak to myself with the same kindness I offer a friend. When I stumble, I help myself up. Gentleness makes me stronger.
I do not need to have everything figured out. I only need to take the next right step. Clarity grows as I move.
I am growing, even when I cannot see it. Roots spread long before the first leaf appears. I am patient with my own becoming.
I let go of what I cannot control. I put my energy where it can make a difference. That is where my peace lives.
I am worthy of love and belonging. I do not have to earn my place in the lives of the people who care about me. I let myself be loved today.
My breath is always with me. When things feel fast, I slow down and breathe. I can return to calm whenever I choose.
I choose progress over perfection. A finished, imperfect thing is better than a perfect one that never begins. Today I will begin.
I am brave enough to try. Even if it does not work out, I will learn something real. Courage is a muscle, and I am building it.
I make room for joy today. I will look for small, bright moments and let myself enjoy them fully. Happiness often hides in ordinary things.
I honor my limits. Saying no to something can be saying yes to myself. My boundaries protect what matters most.
I am more than my mistakes. I own them, I learn from them, and I let them go. They are chapters, not my whole story.
I bring something good to the world simply by being myself. My kindness matters. My presence makes a difference to someone.
I am grateful for this body that carries me through every day. I will care for it with food, movement and rest. It deserves my kindness.
I release the need to compare my journey with anyone else’s. My path is my own, and it is unfolding at the right pace. I walk it with pride.
Today I focus on what I can give, not what I lack. There is always something I can offer: a kind word, my attention, my effort. Giving fills me up too.
I am capable of hard things. I have done them before. I will meet today’s challenges one at a time.
My feelings are valid, and I let myself feel them. I do not have to fix everything right away. Understanding comes when I give it space.
I welcome change as a chance to grow. Not every change is easy, but each one can teach me something. I adapt, and I keep going.
I am at peace with where I am. I can want more for my life and still appreciate this moment. Both can be true.
I deserve the same patience I give to others. I will not rush my healing. Good things grow at their own pace.
I can create something today, however small. A meal, a note, a sketch, a kind gesture. Making things reminds me of my own spark.
I choose thoughts that lift me up. When worry knocks, I can answer with hope. My mind is a garden, and I decide what to plant.
I am surrounded by more support than I sometimes notice. I am allowed to ask for help. Reaching out is a sign of strength.
I keep my promises to myself. Each small promise kept builds my trust in who I am. Today I will keep one.
I am open to good surprises. Not everything unexpected is a problem. Some of today’s best moments have not happened yet.
I let my light shine without apology. I do not need to shrink to make others comfortable. The world needs what I have to offer.
I give myself permission to rest without guilt. A tired mind sees problems as bigger than they are. After rest, I will see clearly again.
I am learning to love the person I am becoming. I celebrate how far I have come. I am excited about where I am going.
I meet this day with an open heart. I will listen more than I judge. Understanding others helps me understand myself.
I am steady, even when life is not. I can bend without breaking. My calm is stronger than any storm.
I forgive myself for what I did not know before. I made the best choices I could with what I had. Now I know more, and I can do better.
I find something to be thankful for in every day. Gratitude turns what I have into enough. Today I will name three good things.
I am in charge of how I respond. Others may set the tone, but I choose my words and actions. I will respond with care.
I celebrate other people’s wins without feeling smaller. There is enough good in the world for all of us. Their light does not dim mine.
I do one thing at a time, and I do it well. I do not need to carry the whole week today. This moment is all I need to handle.
I am becoming stronger through every challenge. What once felt impossible now feels familiar. I am proof that people grow.
I say yes to what lights me up. I make time for the people and passions that bring me alive. My joy is worth protecting.
I trust that things can work out. I have seen hard seasons turn into better ones. Hope is a choice I make again today.
I let go of yesterday’s worries. Today has its own possibilities. I greet it with curiosity instead of dread.
I treat my dreams with respect. They are not silly; they are directions. I will take one small step toward one today.
I am kind to the people around me, and kind to myself. Kindness costs nothing and changes everything. I will spread a little today.
My past does not define my future. Every day I write a new page. I choose to make this one a good one.
I take up space with confidence. My voice deserves to be heard. I speak up for what matters to me.
I am at home in my own company. Quiet moments with myself are a gift. In stillness, I hear what I need.
I end this day knowing I did what I could. Whatever was left undone can wait for tomorrow. I rest with a peaceful heart.
Try box breathing: breathe in for four counts, hold for four, breathe out for four, and hold for four. Repeat it four times and notice your shoulders drop.
Name five things you can see, four you can hear, three you can touch, two you can smell and one you can taste. It brings your mind back to the room you are in.
Make your exhale longer than your inhale. Breathe in for four counts and out for six. A slower out-breath tells your body it is safe to relax.
Write down everything on your mind, then circle just one thing you can do today. The rest can wait on the page instead of in your head.
Unclench your jaw, drop your shoulders and soften your hands. Stress often hides in the body before we notice it in the mind.
Step outside for five minutes. Look at the sky, feel the air and let your eyes rest on something far away.
Ask yourself: will this matter in a week? A month? A year? Many worries shrink when you see them from a distance.
Drink a glass of water slowly. Simple care for your body can steady your mind more than you expect.
Put your phone face down for ten minutes. Let your attention rest on one thing at a time.
Text someone you trust, even just to say hello. Connection is one of the strongest antidotes to stress.
Break a big task into the smallest possible first step, like opening the document or putting on your shoes. Starting is often the hardest part.
Place a hand on your chest and feel it rise and fall. Say quietly to yourself, "This is a hard moment, and I can get through it."
Move for a few minutes: stretch, walk, dance in the kitchen. Movement helps your body use up the energy that stress creates.
Tense your shoulders up to your ears, hold for five seconds, then let them fall. Do the same with your fists and your feet.
Notice the story you are telling yourself. Is it a fact, or a fear? Treat fears gently, but do not mistake them for facts.
Think of one thing that went right today, however small. Stress narrows your view; gratitude widens it again.
Give your worry a time slot. Set aside fifteen minutes later today to think it through, and when it comes up before then, remind yourself it has an appointment.
Lower the bar for today. Doing the essentials and resting is a perfectly good day.
Listen to one song you love with your eyes closed, and do nothing else. Let it be the whole of your attention for three minutes.
Tidy one small space, like a drawer, your desk or a single shelf. A little order outside can bring a little order inside.
If your thoughts are racing, say them out loud or write them down. Thoughts are easier to sort once they are outside your head.
Ask yourself what you would tell a friend in your situation. Then offer yourself the same advice, in the same kind voice.
Before bed, write down tomorrow’s top three tasks. Your mind can let go more easily once it knows nothing will be forgotten.
Warm your hands under running water or around a mug, and focus on the warmth. Simple sensations can anchor a busy mind.
Remember that you do not have to solve everything tonight. Sleep, food and a little time often make a problem smaller.
Isn’t it splendid to think of all the things there are to find out about?
Tomorrow is a new day with no mistakes in it yet.
I’m so glad I live in a world where there are Octobers.
It’s been my experience that you can nearly always enjoy things if you make up your mind firmly that you will.
It is a fair, even-handed, noble adjustment of things, that while there is infection in disease and sorrow, there is nothing in the world so irresistibly contagious as laughter and good-humour.
I am as light as a feather, I am as happy as an angel, I am as merry as a schoolboy.
Have regular hours for work and play; make each day both useful and pleasant.
It takes a heap o’ livin’ in a house t’ make it home.
The morning, which is the most memorable season of the day, is the awakening hour.
Heaven is under our feet as well as over our heads.
I exist as I am, that is enough.
To me every hour of the light and dark is a miracle, Every cubic inch of space is a miracle.
Be thankful, therefore, for the least benefit and thou shalt be worthy to receive greater.
We need so to view the world as to combine an idea of wonder and an idea of welcome.
We need to be happy in this wonderland without once being merely comfortable.
Oh, you’ll not be any poorer if you smile along your way, And your lot will not be harder for the kindly things you say.
Can the grumbler labor better than the cheerful fellow can?
Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.
Whoso would be a man must be a nonconformist.
A foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds.
Nothing great was ever achieved without enthusiasm.
To believe your own thought, to believe that what is true for you in your private heart is true for all men,—that is genius.
The only way to have a friend is to be one.
A friend is a person with whom I may be sincere.
The voyage of the best ship is a zigzag line of a hundred tacks.
To fill the hour,—that is happiness.
If one advances confidently in the direction of his dreams, and endeavors to live the life which he has imagined, he will meet with a success unexpected in common hours.
If you have built castles in the air, your work need not be lost; that is where they should be. Now put the foundations under them.
Simplify, simplify.

I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach, and not, when I came to die, discover that I had not lived.
If a man does not keep pace with his companions, perhaps it is because he hears a different drummer. Let him step to the music which he hears, however measured or far away.
The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation.
Only that day dawns to which we are awake. There is more day to dawn. The sun is but a morning star.
I have, as it were, my own sun and moon and stars, and a little world all to myself.
I love a broad margin to my life.
Optimism is the faith that leads to achievement. Nothing can be done without hope.
Although the world is full of suffering, it is full also of the overcoming of it.
Everything has its wonders, even darkness and silence, and I learn, whatever state I may be in, therein to be content.
The best and most beautiful things in the world cannot be seen nor even touched, but just felt in the heart.
Afoot and light-hearted I take to the open road, Healthy, free, the world before me.
I am large, I contain multitudes.
I believe a leaf of grass is no less than the journey-work of the stars.
Hope is the thing with feathers That perches in the soul, And sings the tune without the words, And never stops at all.
If I can stop one heart from breaking, I shall not live in vain.
That I shall love alway, I offer thee That love is life, And life hath immortality.
He who knows other men is discerning; he who knows himself is intelligent.
The journey of a thousand li commenced with a single step.
There is nothing in the world more soft and weak than water, and yet for attacking things that are firm and strong there is nothing that can take precedence of it.
Is it not pleasant to learn with a constant perseverance and application?
Learning without thought is labour lost; thought without learning is perilous.
When we see men of worth, we should think of equalling them; when we see men of a contrary character, we should turn inwards and examine ourselves.
To see what is right and not to do it is want of courage.
When you know a thing, to hold that you know it; and when you do not know a thing, to allow that you do not know it;—this is knowledge.
Let us endeavor so to live that when we come to die even the undertaker will be sorry.
Few things are harder to put up with than the annoyance of a good example.
Habit is habit, and not to be flung out of the window by any man, but coaxed down-stairs a step at a time.
When angry, count four; when very angry, swear.

Behold, the fool saith, "Put not all thine eggs in the one basket"—which is but a manner of saying, "Scatter your money and your attention;" but the wise man saith, "Put all your eggs in the one basket and—WATCH THAT BASKET."
Grief can take care of itself; but to get the full value of a joy you must have somebody to divide it with.
Tell the truth or trump—but get the trick.
It is difference of opinion that makes horse-races.
Each person is born to one possession which outvalues all his others—his last breath.
Truth is the most valuable thing we have. Let us economize it.
Courage is resistance to fear, mastery of fear—not absence of fear.
Man is the Only Animal that Blushes. Or needs to.
There are several good protections against temptations, but the surest is cowardice.
Be careless in your dress if you must, but keep a tidy soul.
The man with a new idea is a Crank until the idea succeeds.
Truth is stranger than fiction, but it is because Fiction is obliged to stick to possibilities; Truth isn’t.
Let us be thankful for the fools. But for them the rest of us could not succeed.
Work consists of whatever a body is obliged to do, and that Play consists of whatever a body is not obliged to do.
I can resist everything except temptation.
We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.
Experience is the name every one gives to their mistakes.
The truth is rarely pure and never simple.
I never travel without my diary. One should always have something sensational to read in the train.
To lose one parent, Mr. Worthing, may be regarded as a misfortune; to lose both looks like carelessness.
There is only one thing in the world worse than being talked about, and that is not being talked about.
The only way to get rid of a temptation is to yield to it.
Nowadays people know the price of everything and the value of nothing.
Why, sometimes I’ve believed as many as six impossible things before breakfast.
"Begin at the beginning," the King said gravely, "and go on till you come to the end: then stop."
"Curiouser and curiouser!" cried Alice.
It’s no use going back to yesterday, because I was a different person then.
"Take some more tea," the March Hare said to Alice, very earnestly. "I’ve had nothing yet," Alice replied in an offended tone, "so I can’t take more."
It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife.
For what do we live, but to make sport for our neighbours, and laugh at them in our turn?
Angels can fly because they can take themselves lightly.
So convenient a thing it is to be a reasonable creature, since it enables one to find or make a reason for everything one has a mind to do.
With the first word I used intelligently, I learned to live, to think, to hope.
I have had a glimpse of the shore, and can now live by the hope of reaching it.
The world is sown with good; but unless I turn my glad thoughts into practical living and till my own field, I cannot reap a kernel of the good.
I am never discouraged by absence of good. I never can be argued into hopelessness.
Nay, the desire and will to work is optimism itself.
I long to accomplish a great and noble task; but it is my chief duty and joy to accomplish humble tasks as though they were great and noble.
My optimism, then, does not rest on the absence of evil, but on a glad belief in the preponderance of good and a willing effort always to coöperate with the good, that it may prevail.
To what is good I open the doors of my being, and jealously shut them against what is bad.
Love is not love Which alters when it alteration finds, Or bends with the remover to remove.
The course of true love never did run smooth.
Love looks not with the eyes, but with the mind; And therefore is wing’d Cupid painted blind.
Love all, trust a few, Do wrong to none.
My bounty is as boundless as the sea, My love as deep; the more I give to thee, The more I have, for both are infinite.
Doubt thou the stars are fire, Doubt that the sun doth move, Doubt truth to be a liar, But never doubt I love.
So long as men can breathe, or eyes can see, So long lives this, and this gives life to thee.
How do I love thee? Let me count the ways. I love thee to the depth and breadth and height My soul can reach.
I love thee with the breath, Smiles, tears, of all my life!
Love gives naught but itself and takes naught but from itself. Love possesses not nor would it be possessed; For love is sufficient unto love.
Let there be spaces in your togetherness, And let the winds of the heavens dance between you.
Love one another, but make not a bond of love: Let it rather be a moving sea between the shores of your souls.
You give but little when you give of your possessions. It is when you give of yourself that you truly give.
The deeper that sorrow carves into your being, the more joy you can contain.
And let your best be for your friend.
Work is love made visible.
You will find as you look back upon your life that the moments that stand out, the moments when you have really lived, are the moments when you have done things in a spirit of love.
quotes.s: The Greatest Thing in the World

quotes.t: Whatever our souls are made of, his and mine are the same.
I am no bird; and no net ensnares me: I am a free human being with an independent will.
I will honour Christmas in my heart, and try to keep it all the year.
It is a far, far better thing that I do, than I have ever done.
He that has once done you a kindness will be more ready to do you another, than he whom you yourself have obliged.
I’m not afraid of storms, for I’m learning how to sail my ship.
Love is the only thing that we can carry with us when we go, and it makes the end so easy.
For Mercy has a human heart, Pity a human face, And Love, the human form divine, And Peace, the human dress.
quotes.s: Songs of Innocence and of Experience

quotes.t: Love is a great thing, a good above all others, which alone maketh every heavy burden light, and equaliseth every inequality.
The quality of mercy is not strain’d, It droppeth as the gentle rain from heaven Upon the place beneath. It is twice blest: It blesseth him that gives and him that takes.
How far that little candle throws his beams! So shines a good deed in a naughty world.
True success lies in acting well your part, and this every one can do.
You cannot long fight successfully against your aspirations.
Let nothing tempt you or swerve you a hair’s breadth from your aim, and you will win.
The world is full of people who are "almost a success." They stop just this side of success.
Give your life, your energy, your enthusiasm, all to the highest work of which you are capable.
Success is jealous of scattered energies.
Form a plan; have an object; then work for it, learn all you can about it, and you will be sure to succeed.
Success is the child of two very plain parents—punctuality and accuracy.
Doing a deed is like sowing a seed: if not done at just the right time it will be forever out of season.
With most people the early morning hour becomes the test of the day’s success.
A few minutes often makes all the difference between victory and defeat, success and failure.
Sadness gives place to joy, despair to hope, and disheartenment to encouragement.
The ability to cultivate friends is a powerful aid to success.
The current will not set toward you until it goes out from you.
Bees will not sting a man smeared with honey.
Character is power, and is the best advertisement in the world.
Beauty of life and character, as in art, has no sharp angles.
You have your own special place and work.
The present time is the raw material out of which we make whatever we will.
Do not brood over the past, or dream of the future, but seize the instant and get your lesson from the hour.
A lowly beginning is no bar to a great career.
They are ordinary people, but of extraordinary persistence and perseverance.
If instinct and heart ask for carpentry, be a carpenter; if for medicine, be a physician.
Our doubts are traitors, And make us lose the good we oft might win, By fearing to attempt.
Cowards die many times before their deaths; The valiant never taste of death but once.
Be not afraid of greatness. Some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon ’em.
This above all: to thine own self be true, And it must follow, as the night the day, Thou canst not then be false to any man.
We know what we are, but know not what we may be.
There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.
All the world’s a stage, And all the men and women merely players.
A merry heart goes all the day, Your sad tires in a mile-a.
The miserable have no other medicine But only hope.
It is rather for us to be here dedicated to the great task remaining before us.
I would always rather be happy than dignified.
All right, then, I’ll go to hell.
Insist on yourself; never imitate.
In every work of genius we recognize our own rejected thoughts; they come back to us with a certain alienated majesty.
Every great man is a unique.
The soul created the arts wherever they have flourished.
People wish to be settled; only as far as they are unsettled is there any hope for them.
Life only avails, not the having lived.
Nothing is at last sacred but the integrity of your own mind.
I celebrate myself, and sing myself.
Do I contradict myself? Very well then I contradict myself, (I am large, I contain multitudes.)
The powerful play goes on, and you may contribute a verse.
O me! O life! of the questions of these recurring.
Tiger, tiger, burning bright In the forests of the night, What immortal hand or eye Could frame thy fearful symmetry?
quotes.s: Songs of Innocence and of Experience

quotes.t: Be rather the Mungo Park, the Lewis and Clarke and Frobisher, of your own streams and oceans; explore your own higher latitudes.
However mean your life is, meet it and live it; do not shun it and call it hard names.
Love your life, poor as it is.
A man is rich in proportion to the number of things which he can afford to let alone.
Time is but the stream I go a-fishing in.
Success is counted sweetest By those who ne’er succeed.
To make a prairie it takes a clover and one bee, One clover, and a bee, And revery.
It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.
Greatness consists not in the holding of some future office, but really consists in doing great deeds with little means and the accomplishment of vast purposes from the private ranks of life.
He who can give to this city better streets and better sidewalks, better schools and more colleges, more happiness and more civilization, more of God, he will be great anywhere.
Your children are not your children. They are the sons and daughters of Life’s longing for itself.
Your pain is the breaking of the shell that encloses your understanding.
Beauty is eternity gazing at itself in a mirror.
Life and death are one, even as the river and the sea are one.
Say not, "I have found the truth," but rather, "I have found a truth."
To wake at dawn with a winged heart and give thanks for another day of loving.
Knowledge is love and light and vision.
It is not eminent talent that is required to ensure success in any pursuit, so much as purpose,—not merely the power to achieve, but the will to labour energetically and perseveringly.
We learn wisdom from failure much more than from success.
He who never made a mistake never made a discovery.
Never value anything as profitable to thyself which shall compel thee to break thy promise, to lose thy self-respect.
It is in thy power whenever thou shalt choose to retire into thyself.
I like good strong words that mean something.
I want to do something splendid before I go into my castle, something heroic or wonderful that won’t be forgotten after I’m dead.
There are many things from which I might have derived good, by which I have not profited, I dare say.
I declare after all there is no enjoyment like reading!
O Wind, If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?
Wild Spirit, which art moving everywhere; Destroyer and preserver; hear, oh hear!
Season of mists and mellow fruitfulness, Close bosom-friend of the maturing sun.
Where are the songs of Spring? Ay, where are they? Think not of them, thou hast thy music too.
Ring out the old, ring in the new, Ring, happy bells, across the snow: The year is going, let him go; Ring out the false, ring in the true.
Ring out, wild bells, to the wild sky, The flying cloud, the frosty light: The year is dying in the night; Ring out, wild bells, and let him die.
Ring in the valiant man and free, The larger heart, the kindlier hand.
’Tis better to have loved and lost Than never to have loved at all.
I heard the bells on Christmas Day Their old, familiar carols play, And wild and sweet The words repeat Of peace on earth, good-will to men!
Then pealed the bells more loud and deep: "God is not dead; nor doth he sleep!"
Lives of great men all remind us We can make our lives sublime, And, departing, leave behind us Footprints on the sands of time.
Let us, then, be up and doing, With a heart for any fate; Still achieving, still pursuing, Learn to labor and to wait.
Be still, sad heart! and cease repining; Behind the clouds is the sun still shining; Thy fate is the common fate of all, Into each life some rain must fall.
Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day? Thou art more lovely and more temperate.
Now is the winter of our discontent Made glorious summer by this son of York.
At Christmas I no more desire a rose Than wish a snow in May’s new-fangled shows, But like of each thing that in season grows.
Blow, blow, thou winter wind, Thou art not so unkind As man’s ingratitude.
Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May, And summer’s lease hath all too short a date.
"God bless us every one!" said Tiny Tim, the last of all.
I will live in the Past, the Present, and the Future. The Spirits of all Three shall strive within me.
The first sparrow of spring! The year beginning with younger hope than ever!
Walden was dead and is alive again.
A light exists in spring Not present on the year At any other period.
I sat in my sunny doorway from sunrise till noon, rapt in a revery, amidst the pines and hickories and sumachs, in undisturbed solitude and stillness.
I withdrew yet farther into my shell, and endeavored to keep a bright fire both within my house and within my breast.
And could you keep your heart in wonder at the daily miracles of your life, your pain would not seem less wondrous than your joy.
The universe is transformation: life is opinion.
Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if thou wilt ever dig.
If thou art pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs thee, but thy own judgment about it.
Always bear this in mind; and another thing too, that very little indeed is necessary for living a happy life.
No longer talk at all about the kind of man that a good man ought to be, but be such.
And so that which is a hindrance is made a furtherance to an act; and that which is an obstacle on the road helps us on this road.
Let not future things disturb thee, for thou wilt come to them, if it shall be necessary, having with thee the same reason which now thou usest for present things.
Be like the promontory against which the waves continually break, but it stands firm and tames the fury of the water around it.
Such as are thy habitual thoughts, such also will be the character of thy mind; for the soul is dyed by the thoughts.
In the morning when thou risest unwillingly, let this thought be present,—I am rising to the work of a human being.
Nothing happens to any man which he is not formed by nature to bear.
Confine thyself to the present.
Retire into thyself.
The art of life is more like the wrestler’s art than the dancer’s, in respect of this, that it should stand ready and firm to meet onsets which are sudden and unexpected.
Do not act as if thou wert going to live ten thousand years.
How much trouble he avoids who does not look to see what his neighbor says or does or thinks, but only to what he does himself, that it may be just and pure.
Adapt thyself to the things with which thy lot has been cast: and the men among whom thou hast received thy portion, love them, but do it truly.
The perfection of moral character consists in this, in passing every day as the last, and in being neither violently excited nor torpid nor playing the hypocrite.
The best way of avenging thyself is not to become like the wrong-doer.
Loss is nothing else than change.
Take away then, when thou choosest, thy opinion, and like a mariner who has doubled the promontory, thou wilt find calm, everything stable, and a waveless bay.
Love the art, poor as it may be, which thou hast learned, and be content with it.
Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things.
There are things which are within our power, and there are things which are beyond our power.
Demand not that events should happen as you wish; but wish them to happen as they do happen, and you will go on well.
If you would improve, be content to be thought foolish and dull with regard to externals.
Nothing great, said Epictetus, is produced suddenly, since not even the grape or the fig is.
If you say to me now that you want a fig, I will answer to you that it requires time: let it flower first, then put forth fruit, and then ripen.
It is circumstances (difficulties) which show what men are.
Failure in any good cause is, however, honourable, whilst success in any bad cause is merely infamous.
It is the diligent hand and head alone that maketh rich—in self-culture, growth in wisdom, and in business.
Labour is not only a necessity and a duty, but a blessing: only the idler feels it to be a curse.
Certain it is that no bread eaten by man is so sweet as that earned by his own labour, whether bodily or mental.
Don’t wait for extraordinary opportunities.
Weak men wait for opportunities, strong men make them.

verses.kjv: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
verses.web: Yahweh is my shepherd: I shall lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.

verses.kjv: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
verses.web: Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.

verses.kjv: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
verses.web: "Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I will be exalted in the earth."

verses.kjv: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
verses.web: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.

verses.kjv: For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
verses.web: For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.

verses.kjv: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
verses.web: This is the day that Yahweh has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it!

verses.kjv: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name. For the LORD is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations.
verses.web: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, into his courts with praise. Give thanks to him, and bless his name. For Yahweh is good. His loving kindness endures forever, his faithfulness to all generations.

verses.kjv: O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
verses.web: Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever.

verses.kjv: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
verses.web: Yahweh is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? Yahweh is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?

verses.kjv: The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped: therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth; and with my song will I praise him.
verses.web: Yahweh is my strength and my shield. My heart has trusted in him, and I am helped. Therefore my heart greatly rejoices. With my song I will thank him.

verses.kjv: Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.
verses.web: Cast your burden on Yahweh, and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.

verses.kjv: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.
verses.web: In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you, Yahweh alone, make me live in safety.

verses.kjv: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
verses.web: Yahweh is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.

verses.kjv: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
verses.web: My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.

verses.kjv: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
verses.web: So teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.

verses.kjv: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
verses.web: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.

verses.kjv: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth.
verses.web: I will lift up my eyes to the hills. Where does my help come from? My help comes from Yahweh, who made heaven and earth.

verses.kjv: The LORD shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore.
verses.web: Yahweh will keep your going out and your coming in, from this time forth, and forevermore.

verses.kjv: The LORD hath done great things for us; whereof we are glad.
verses.web: Yahweh has done great things for us, and we are glad.

verses.kjv: O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
verses.web: Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good; for his loving kindness endures forever.

verses.kjv: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
verses.web: See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity!

verses.kjv: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.
verses.web: I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well.

verses.kjv: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
verses.web: He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds.

verses.kjv: Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him: fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way, because of the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass.
verses.web: Rest in Yahweh, and wait patiently for him. Don’t fret because of him who prospers in his way, because of the man who makes wicked plots happen.

verses.kjv: Delight thyself also in the LORD: and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart. Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.
verses.web: Also delight yourself in Yahweh, and he will give you the desires of your heart. Commit your way to Yahweh. Trust also in him, and he will do this:

verses.kjv: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
verses.web: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.

verses.kjv: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
verses.web: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.

verses.kjv: A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones.
verses.web: A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.

verses.kjv: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
verses.web: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

verses.kjv: Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.
verses.web: Commit your deeds to Yahweh, and your plans shall succeed.

verses.kjv: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
verses.web: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.

verses.kjv: A man’s heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps.
verses.web: A man’s heart plans his course, but Yahweh directs his steps.

verses.kjv: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
verses.web: The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.

verses.kjv: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:
verses.web: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise;

verses.kjv: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.
verses.web: The plans of the diligent surely lead to profit; and everyone who is hasty surely rushes to poverty.

verses.kjv: Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.
verses.web: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.

verses.kjv: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
verses.web: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; those who love it will eat its fruit.

verses.kjv: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.
verses.web: The wicked flee when no one pursues; but the righteous are as bold as a lion.

verses.kjv: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
verses.web: For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:

verses.kjv: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
verses.web: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;

verses.kjv: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.
verses.web: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.

verses.kjv: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.
verses.web: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.

verses.kjv: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.
verses.web: Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned. Friends

verses.kjv: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
verses.web: But those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.

verses.kjv: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
verses.web: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.

verses.kjv: Remember ye not the former things, neither consider the things of old. Behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall ye not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
verses.web: Don’t remember the former things, and don’t consider the things of old. Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs forth now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.

verses.kjv: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
verses.web: You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.

verses.kjv: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.
verses.web: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.

verses.kjv: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.
verses.web: For to us a child is born. To us a son is given; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

verses.kjv: He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.
verses.web: He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.

verses.kjv: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
verses.web: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, says Yahweh, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope in your latter end.

verses.kjv: It is of the LORD’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
verses.web: [It is of] Yahweh’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn’t fail. They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.

verses.kjv: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
verses.web: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and of good courage. Don’t be afraid, neither be dismayed: for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.

verses.kjv: Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
verses.web: Be strong and of good courage, don’t be afraid, nor be scared of them: for Yahweh your God, he it is who does go with you; he will not fail you, nor forsake you.

verses.kjv: Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our LORD: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the LORD is your strength.
verses.web: Then he said to them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared; for this day is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved; for the joy of Yahweh is your strength.

verses.kjv: The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.
verses.web: Yahweh will fight for you, and you shall be still.

verses.kjv: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
verses.web: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?

verses.kjv: The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.
verses.web: Yahweh, your God, is in the midst of you, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He will rest in his love. He will rejoice over you with singing.

verses.kjv: For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.
verses.web: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will surely come. It won’t delay.

verses.kjv: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
verses.web: "Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart; and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light."

verses.kjv: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
verses.web: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.

verses.kjv: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
verses.web: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?

verses.kjv: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;
verses.web: But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,

verses.kjv: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
verses.web: Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.

verses.kjv: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.
verses.web: Therefore whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.

verses.kjv: But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
verses.web: Looking at them, Jesus said, "With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible."

verses.kjv: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:
verses.web: Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.

verses.kjv: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
verses.web: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.

verses.kjv: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
verses.web: He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said. Come, see the place where the Lord was lying.

verses.kjv: And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
verses.web: The angel said to them, Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people. For there is born to you, this day, in the city of David, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.

verses.kjv: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.
verses.web: "Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men."

verses.kjv: And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.
verses.web: As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them.

verses.kjv: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.
verses.web: "Give, and it will be given to you: good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, will be given to you. For with the same measure you measure it will be measured back to you."

verses.kjv: For with God nothing shall be impossible.
verses.web: For everything spoken by God is possible.

verses.kjv: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
verses.web: For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

verses.kjv: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
verses.web: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another, just like I have loved you; that you also love one another. By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.

verses.kjv: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
verses.web: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, give I to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.

verses.kjv: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
verses.web: I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have oppression; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.

verses.kjv: This is my commandment, That ye love one another, as I have loved you. Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
verses.web: This is my commandment, that you love one another, even as I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.

verses.kjv: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
verses.web: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome it.

verses.kjv: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:
verses.web: Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies.

verses.kjv: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
verses.web: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, to those who are called according to his purpose.

verses.kjv: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.web: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

verses.kjv: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
verses.web: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope, in the power of the Holy Spirit.

verses.kjv: And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope:
verses.web: Not only this, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering works perseverance; and perseverance, proven character; and proven character, hope:

verses.kjv: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.
verses.web: Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.

verses.kjv: Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another;
verses.web: In love of the brothers be tenderly affectionate one to another; in honor preferring one another;

verses.kjv: Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer;
verses.web: rejoicing in hope; enduring in troubles; continuing steadfastly in prayer;

verses.kjv: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil;
verses.web: Love is patient and is kind; love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud, doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil;

verses.kjv: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
verses.web: But now faith, hope, and love remain--these three. The greatest of these is love.

verses.kjv: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong. Let all your things be done with charity.
verses.web: Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong! Let all that you do be done in love.

verses.kjv: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
verses.web: He has said to me, "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness." Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.

verses.kjv: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.
verses.web: Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day.

verses.kjv: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
verses.web: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

verses.kjv: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
verses.web: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

verses.kjv: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
verses.web: Let us not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season, if we don’t give up.

verses.kjv: Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
verses.web: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.

verses.kjv: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
verses.web: And be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.

verses.kjv: With all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love;
verses.web: with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love;

verses.kjv: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
verses.web: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

verses.kjv: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
verses.web: I can do all things through Christ, who strengthens me.

verses.kjv: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
verses.web: Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are honorable, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report; if there is any virtue, and if there is any praise, think about these things.

verses.kjv: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
verses.web: Brothers, I don’t regard myself as yet having taken hold, but one thing I do. Forgetting the things which are behind, and stretching forward to the things which are before, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.

verses.kjv: Rejoice in the Lord alway: and again I say, Rejoice.
verses.web: Rejoice in the Lord always! Again I will say, Rejoice!

verses.kjv: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.
verses.web: Not that I speak in respect to lack, for I have learned in whatever state I am, to be content in it.

verses.kjv: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:
verses.web: being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.

verses.kjv: And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men;
verses.web: And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men,

verses.kjv: And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.
verses.web: Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection.

verses.kjv: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.
verses.web: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body; and be thankful.

verses.kjv: Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
verses.web: Rejoice always. Pray without ceasing. In everything give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you.

verses.kjv: Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another, even as also ye do.
verses.web: Therefore exhort one another, and build each other up, even as you also do.

verses.kjv: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
verses.web: For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.

verses.kjv: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:
verses.web: I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.

verses.kjv: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
verses.web: Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.

verses.kjv: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
verses.web: Therefore let us also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,

verses.kjv: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
verses.web: Don’t forget to show hospitality to strangers, for in doing so, some have entertained angels without knowing it.

verses.kjv: My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.
verses.web: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations, knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance. Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.

verses.kjv: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
verses.web: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach; and it will be given to him.

verses.kjv: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:
verses.web: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;

verses.kjv: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
verses.web: casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.

verses.kjv: And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.
verses.web: And above all things be earnest in your love among yourselves, for love covers a multitude of sins.

verses.kjv: Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God. He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.
verses.web: Beloved, let us love one another, for love is of God; and everyone who loves is born of God, and knows God. He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love.

verses.kjv: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.
verses.web: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment. He who fears is not made perfect in love.

verses.kjv: We love him, because he first loved us.
verses.web: We love Him, because he first loved us.

verses.kjv: My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth.
verses.web: My little children, let’s not love in word only, neither with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.

verses.kjv: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
verses.web: He will wipe away from them every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain, any more. The first things have passed away.
